i was testing about this as well on both gemini-3.1-pro and gemini-3-flash, and after some digging with gemini pro itself, it asserted:

The root cause is a known limitation of the Copilot session.send API pipeline: It completely ignores system instructions that
 enforce schema.

 When Vercel AI SDK calls generateObject in mode: 'json', it injects a system prompt asking the model to strictly follow your
 provided JSON schema (which in our script was {"recipe": {"name": "...", "ingredients": [...]}}).

 But look at what Gemini actually returns:

 ```json
   {
     "title": "Toast",
     "ingredients": [
       "1 slice of bread"
     ],
     "instructions": [
       "Place the bread in a toaster and heat until golden brown."
     ]
   }
 ```

 It outputs valid JSON, but it invents its own schema (title, ingredients as an array of strings, instructions) completely
 ignoring the schema the AI SDK requested. Because the fields don't match the Zod schema exactly, the SDK throws a
 AI_NoObjectGeneratedError: response did not match schema.

 As confirmed by my Exa search across the github/copilot-sdk issues, the GitHub Copilot API currently lacks a response_format:
 { type: "json_schema" } field on the backend (Issue #41 / #857). Until GitHub adds native structured_outputs: true support to
 their proxy, any model routed through Copilot (including gemini-3.1-pro-preview) will be "deaf" to strict schema enforcement.
Closing to revise and resubmit.

@otherippo as far as I understand `docker sandbox` is an entirely different technology/product under the Docker brand (microVM and not container). The main selling point seems to be that the coding agents can safely run docker itself inside the microVM, which is not possible inside a container. It also transparently injects credentials into requests so that the agent cannot even leak it's own credentials if it were tricked to.
